correctness.rationale: The universal vertex cannot be zero because it has no vertex at distance two. Once positive, it makes totality automatic if there is a positive peripheral vertex. A peripheral zero can be defended exactly from another petal. Partitioning by zero, one, or at least two petals containing a 2 gives respectively z^M, the sum of D_i times the other B_j, and the complement of the unrestricted zero- and one-defender-petal assignments. All cases have a positive peripheral vertex, so the center contributes z+z^2 independently. At z=1 the one-defender-petal correction D_i-C_i gives 2^(s_i+1)-3^s_i-1. The least peripheral weights are M, s_i+1 and 4 in the respective strata, and the last is realized because q>=2. Thus weight four requires a size-two petal and a center 1; when every petal has size at least three, weight five requires a center 1 and either a single size-three petal with one 2 or a 2 in each of two petals. The exact multiplicities follow by choosing the positions of the 2s. Raising a label preserves defense and the positive support condition because of the positive hub. This attains every intermediate weight. An independent BFS/ternary enumeration reproduced all coefficients for (2,2) and (3,3); the general result is proved by the partition, not by this bounded check.

value.rationale: The problem gives a full benchmark for a natural infinite block-graph family under an established graph-labeling invariant. It distinguishes two competing optimal support types and quantifies their contributions for arbitrary mixtures of petal sizes; a scalar minimum or monotonic interval argument alone would not give those counts or the full distribution.
